purpose: Research queue for families and malware-like tool clusters that should be considered for Malware Lineage Atlas coverage.

priority_legend.P0: Core iconic or structurally important family. Add before broad long tail.
priority_legend.P1: High-value family with strong public source availability.
priority_legend.P2: Useful breadth or active relevance. Add after category spine is stronger.

items.name: GameOver ZeuS
items.reason: Major ZeuS descendant and public law-enforcement case. Good bridge between banking malware, botnet operations, and CryptoLocker distribution.

items.name: Ursnif
items.reason: Long-running banking malware with public lineage and alias complexity. Good test case for alias and fork discipline.

items.name: Zloader
items.reason: Frequently described in relation to ZeuS lineage. Needs careful typing as fork, derivative, or related family depending on source wording.

items.name: Locky
items.reason: Iconic ransomware family tied to major botnet and downloader ecosystems.

items.name: Necurs
items.reason: Major spam/distribution botnet for Locky, Dridex, and related campaigns.

items.name: Hermes
items.reason: Commonly discussed in Ryuk lineage context. Needs reverse-engineering evidence before promoting to derivation.

items.name: Maze
items.reason: Important ransomware ecosystem predecessor for double extortion and later rebrand/operator-continuity claims.

items.name: Egregor
items.reason: High-value Maze successor/rebrand lead with public reporting.

items.name: BitPaymer
items.reason: Key Evil Corp ransomware family with links to Dridex ecosystem.

items.name: DoppelPaymer
items.reason: Often discussed as related to BitPaymer and Evil Corp operations.

items.name: WastedLocker
items.reason: Evil Corp ransomware with useful operator/ecosystem edges.

items.name: RansomHub
items.reason: Current high-activity ransomware ecosystem. Good active-coverage candidate, but lineage claims need caution.

items.name: Hive
items.reason: Major RaaS with public takedown and operator/ecosystem reporting.

items.name: Royal
items.reason: Important Conti-adjacent operator continuity candidate. Needs careful split between Royal and BlackSuit.

items.name: BlackSuit
items.reason: Royal/BlackSuit relationship is a strong candidate for tentative code or rebrand modeling.

items.name: Akira
items.reason: Current ransomware family with public advisories and possible Conti ecosystem leads.

items.name: Play
items.reason: Current high-volume ransomware family with public advisories.

items.name: Babuk
items.reason: Source leak influenced later ESXi/Linux lockers. Good case for code reuse vs builder reuse.

items.name: Cerber
items.reason: Iconic RaaS era family. Helps historical coverage.

items.name: Dharma
items.reason: Long-running family with variant and alias complexity.

items.name: Phobos
items.reason: Often discussed in relation to Dharma/Crysis ecosystem. Needs exact public evidence.

items.name: STOP
items.reason: Mass-market ransomware with many variants. Useful for variant/taxonomy modeling.

items.name: Bumblebee
items.reason: Loader that appeared in crimeware ecosystem after BazarLoader disruption. Good replacement-vs-lineage test.

items.name: BazarLoader
items.reason: TrickBot/Conti ecosystem loader with public reporting.

items.name: SmokeLoader
items.reason: Long-running loader with public Operation Endgame context.

items.name: GootLoader
items.reason: Important initial access loader with public reporting.

items.name: Latrodectus
items.reason: Current loader with public links to IcedID operators or replacement narratives.

items.name: DarkGate
items.reason: Current loader/RAT-adjacent malware with broad public reporting.

items.name: Agent Tesla
items.reason: Iconic commodity stealer with broad public coverage.

items.name: FormBook
items.reason: Commodity stealer with XLoader lineage/continuity claims.

items.name: XLoader
items.reason: Frequently reported as FormBook successor/cross-platform variant. Needs careful typing.

items.name: Snake Keylogger
items.reason: Common commodity infostealer with public reporting.

items.name: DarkComet
items.reason: Iconic public RAT. Useful for historical RAT cluster coverage.

items.name: njRAT
items.reason: Iconic commodity RAT with many variants and public reporting.

items.name: AsyncRAT
items.reason: Open-source RAT frequently reused. Good for codebase/tooling distinction.

items.name: QuasarRAT
items.reason: Open-source RAT base for multiple variants. Good for fork and derivative modeling.

items.name: NanoCore
items.reason: Commodity RAT with public law-enforcement and research coverage.

items.name: Gh0st RAT
items.reason: Historic RAT with source leak/derivative ecosystem. Good code-family cluster candidate.

items.name: Poison Ivy
items.reason: Historic RAT heavily used in APT reporting.

items.name: Ramnit
items.reason: Historic botnet/banker with public takedown and lineage context.

items.name: Gamarue
items.reason: Major botnet with public takedown and wide distribution ecosystem.

items.name: Kelihos
items.reason: Historic botnet with public takedown. Useful for botnet category depth.

items.name: Sality
items.reason: Long-running malware/botnet family. Useful historical coverage.

items.name: ZeroAccess
items.reason: Iconic rootkit/botnet family. Helps sparse rootkit coverage.

items.name: TDSS
items.reason: Major bootkit/rootkit family with lineage and variant complexity.

items.name: Necurs rootkit
items.reason: Could model Necurs rootkit/botnet capabilities carefully if source wording supports it.

items.name: Flame
items.reason: Iconic espionage platform with public research links to Stuxnet ecosystem.

items.name: Gauss
items.reason: Flame-linked espionage malware. Useful for high-confidence historical cluster.

items.name: Triton
items.reason: Iconic ICS-targeting malware for safety-system manipulation and disruption.

items.name: Industroyer2
items.reason: Directly relevant successor/variant candidate for Industroyer.

items.name: HermeticWiper
items.reason: Major Ukraine destructive malware. Useful wiper category spine.

items.name: CaddyWiper
items.reason: Ukraine destructive malware with public technical reporting.

items.name: WhisperGate
items.reason: Ukraine destructive malware with public reporting. Keep behavior/ecosystem separate from code lineage.

items.name: AcidRain
items.reason: Viasat-related wiper with public research and possible VPNFilter relationship leads.

items.name: VPNFilter
items.reason: Router malware with public government and vendor research. Potential links to BlackEnergy/Sandworm context need caution.

items.name: Gafgyt
items.reason: Major IoT botnet family. Complements Mirai/Satori/Mozi.

items.name: Hajime
items.reason: IoT botnet frequently compared with Mirai. Good behavior/ecosystem edge candidate.

items.name: Emotet Epochs
items.reason: Could be modeled later as campaigns or infrastructure epochs rather than separate families.
